140	- **Never forget output mapping on End nodes** — every `out` variable in `variables.globals` must have a `source` expression in every reachable End node's `outputs`. Missing mappings cause silent runtime failures.
141	- **Never update `in` variables** — only `inout` variables can be modified via `variableUpdates`. Input variables are read-only after flow start.
142	- **Never reference parent-scope `$vars` inside a subflow** — subflows have isolated scope. Pass values explicitly via subflow inputs.
143	- **Never use `core.action.http` (v1)** — the v1 node is deprecated for all HTTP requests (both connector-authenticated and manual). For connector-auth, v1's `authenticationType: "connection"` input does not pass IS credentials at runtime. Use `core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request) for every HTTP node. See [http/planning.md](references/plugins/http/planning.md).
144	- **Never hand-write `definitions[]` or `inputs.*` for managed HTTP nodes** — use `uip maestro flow node add` (with `--input` for `branches` / `timeout` / `retryCount`) and `uip maestro flow node configure` (for `inputs.detail`). These are the only supported authoring paths. Hand-written `definitions[]` strips required manifest fields; hand-written `inputs.detail` misses `essentialConfiguration` and fails at runtime. See [http/impl.md](references/plugins/http/impl.md).
145	- **Never write `$vars.X` (or `$metadata.X`, `$self.X`) without `=js:` in value fields** — `flow validate` flags this as MST-9107. See rule #11 above and [shared/node-output-wiring.md](../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the per-node-type field reference.
146	- **Never reuse a reference ID (mailbox folder, Slack channel, Jira project, Google Sheet, etc.) from a prior flow or session** — reference IDs are scoped to the specific authenticated account behind the connection. A `parentFolderId` from one Outlook mailbox is invalid in another; a Slack channel ID from one workspace is invalid in another. A reused ID passes `flow validate` and `node configure` cleanly, then faults silently at runtime with no resolvable error. Always re-resolve via `uip is resources run list <connector-key> <objectName> --connection-id <CURRENT_CONNECTION_ID> --output json` against the connection bound to this flow — do not paste a value you saw in another flow. See [connector/impl.md — Step 4](references/plugins/connector/impl.md) and [connector-trigger/impl.md — Step 3](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md).
147	- **Never include `[*]` literally in a connector `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` key** — `[*]` in `requestFields[].name` is an array marker. Strip it and pass a `=js:` expression returning the array (e.g. `"fields.labels[*]"` → `"fields.labels": "=js:(['a', 'b'])"`). Never a literal JSON array — it validates but does not bind. Supported only when `[*]` is the name suffix; `[*]. See [connector/impl.md — Step 6b](references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the full table including expression-value handling.

33	## Three-turn execution map
34	
35	Steps 0–6 are **logical phases**, not separate turns. A typical greenfield build collapses to **three assistant turns** (universal SKILL.md rule #10). Each step heading below carries a `[T1]` / `[T2]` / `[T3]` tag — emit every tool call inside the same Turn as one assistant message.
36	
37	| Turn | Steps | What you emit in ONE assistant message |
38	|---|---|---|
39	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-execution-map-intro:end-->
40	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:start-->
41	| **T1 — Setup + discovery** | 0, 1, 2, 3 | One chained `Bash` (scaffold + register + pull + `node add` for each CLI-owned node) **+** parallel `Bash` (one `registry get` per OOTB type you'll inline) **+** parallel `Read` (plugin `impl.md`s). **If existing `.uipx` solutions are present, the Step 2 gate fires first in its own turn** — resolve it before this chain. |
42	| **T2 — Read + author** | 4 | One `Read` of the `.flow` **+** a batch of `Edit` calls (or one `Write` if ≥70% of nodes change). Claude Code serializes Edits on the same file, so they don't race |
43	| **T3 — Finalize** | 5, 6 | One chained `Bash` (`node configure && validate && format`). On validate failure: one Edit turn, then re-chain `validate && format` |
44	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:end-->
45	
46	### Batching anti-patterns
47	
48	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:start-->
49	- **One CLI per turn.** Never issue `solution init`, then `cd`, then `flow init` as three separate Bash calls — chain with `&&`, the `cd` included as its own segment. Same for `node configure && validate && format`.
50	- **Sequential `registry get`s.** Emit every `registry get` as a parallel `Bash` in one message alongside the T1 scaffold chain.
51	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:end-->
52	- **Validating after every Edit.** Validate once at the end of T3 (or after a recovery Edit). Intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
53	- **Re-reading the `.flow` every turn.** `Read` once at the start of T2; subsequent `Edit`s in the same conversation don't need re-reading unless an external command (e.g., `node configure`, `format`) rewrites the file between Edits.
54	- **`Edit` in the same turn as a `Bash` that mutates the same file.** Parallel tool calls race — separate them across turns.
55	- **Two parallel `Edit`s anchored to the same byte range.** Same-file Edits serialize in execution order; if Edit N's `old_string` overlaps text that Edit N-1's substitution removed or shifted, Edit N fails with "string not found." Use the [per-array anchor pattern](#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order) — anchor each Edit on its target array's own opening key, never on key order or a shared boundary.

85	## Step 2 — Create a solution, THEN a Flow project inside it **[T1]**
86	
87	> **A Flow project cannot exist outside a solution** (universal rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). Run `uip maestro flow init` (Step 2b) outside a solution and it now **auto-scaffolds** one — `<Project>Solution/<Project>Solution.uipx` with the project nested at `<Project>Solution/<Project>/` (response carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution`). Still scaffold or select the solution first (Step 2a) so you set the solution name yourself rather than the auto `<Project>Solution`, and so discovery is unambiguous. The solution and project names are independent — they need not match. The correct layout is **always** `<Solution>/<Project>/<Project>.flow` (double-nested — see the tree after Step 2c). Passing `--skip-solution-registration` opts out of both auto-scaffold and registration, leaving a bare single-nested layout that fails Studio Web upload and packaging.
88	
89	Check for existing solutions with `find . -maxdepth 2 -type f -name '*.uipx' -print` (each solution is its own folder — `<Solution>/<Solution>.uipx` — so a bare `*.uipx` glob misses them). If any are found, **STOP before the T1 chain — do not run `uip solution init` yet** — and ask the user which solution to use per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md) (rules #5 and #6): one option per discovered `.uipx`, a **"Create a new solution"** option, and **"Something else"** last. Rule #5 owns the ask mechanism (structured `AskUserQuestion` where the runtime offers it, a numbered chat list otherwise, recommended-option fallback when non-interactive) — do not re-specify a tool here. Applies even when the user wants a new solution. If none are found, create a new one automatically.
90	
91	- If the user specifies an existing `.uipx` file path or solution name, use that (skip to Step 2b)
92	- Otherwise, create a new solution (Step 2a)

94	### Canonical T1 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
95	
96	This is the consolidated command that does Steps 2a + 2b + Step 3 + (optionally) one `node add` per CLI-owned node, in one chained Bash. `node add` signature is `<file> <node-type>` (file first):
97	
98	```bash
99	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json \
100	  && cd "<SolutionName>" \
101	  && uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>" --output json \
102	  && cd "<ProjectName>" \
103	  && uip maestro flow registry pull \
104	  && uip maestro flow node add "<ProjectName>.flow" core.action.http.v2 --label "<NodeLabel>" --output json
105	```
106	
107	> **One creation path — never drop the `cd`.** `uip solution init "<SolutionName>"` → `cd "<SolutionName>"` → `uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>"`, one chain. Without the `cd`, `flow init` runs in the old directory and auto-scaffolds a duplicate `<ProjectName>Solution/` (1-node husk). Never let auto-scaffold create the solution. Finish with exactly one `project.uiproj` — delete strays.
108	
109	Tail-append one `node add` per CLI-owned node (`uipath.connector.*`, `uipath.connector.trigger.*`, `core.action.http.v2`). Each `node add` returns the new node `id` in `Data` — capture it from the chained output for T2/T3. Drop the trailing `node add` segment when the flow is OOTB-only.
110	
111	In the SAME assistant message (parallel to this chain): emit one `Bash` per OOTB `registry get <NODE_TYPE>` you'll need in T2 (always `core.control.end` — see Step 4), and parallel `Read` calls for any plugin `impl.md`s you'll consult.
112	
113	> **Older `solution-tool` (< 1.0.0)** used `solution new` (see [.claude/rules/cli-renames.md](../../../../../.claude/rules/cli-renames.md)). If `solution init` returns `unknown command`, substitute `solution new`.
114	
115	The sub-steps below describe what each command in the chain does and how to verify the result.
116	
117	### 2a. Create a new solution
118	
119	```bash
120	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json
121	```
122	
123	Creates `<cwd>/<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx`. **`cd` into the new solution directory before Step 2b.**
124	
125	> **Naming convention:** In **pure greenfield** (no existing solutions), default the solution name to the project name unless the user specifies otherwise. When solutions already exist and the user chooses "Create a new solution", **ask for the new solution's name** — do not reuse the project name (SKILL.md rule #6). The two names are independent.
126	
127	### 2b. Create the Flow project inside the solution folder
128	
129	```bash
130	cd <directory>/<SolutionName> && uip maestro flow init <ProjectName> --output json
131	```
132	
133	The `cd` puts the project inside the solution you just created. Skip it and `flow init` won't find that solution (discovery walks **up**, not down into `<SolutionName>/`) — it auto-scaffolds a **second, separate** `<ProjectName>Solution/` beside your empty `<SolutionName>/`, leaving two solutions. The project no longer single-nests, but `cd` first to land in the right one.
134	
135	> **Bash session state persists across tool calls.** This `cd` is **not scoped to one Bash invocation** — your cwd remains inside `<SolutionName>/` for every subsequent `Bash` call until you `cd` somewhere else. Plan the rest of Step 2 (and Steps 3–6) accordingly: either keep using paths relative to the solution dir, or anchor with `$(pwd)` / the absolute `Data.Path` returned by `flow init`. Do NOT prefix later commands with the original `<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` — that would resolve as `<SolutionName>/<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` and look like a layout bug when it isn't.
136	
137	`--output json` is required so Step 2c can inspect `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` to confirm the project was auto-registered with the parent solution.
138	
139	### 2c. Verify the project is registered in the solution
140	
141	When `uip maestro flow init` is run from inside a solution directory (Step 2b), it **auto-registers** the project with the nearest parent `.uipx`. Run outside any solution, it **auto-scaffolds** `<Project>Solution/` and registers the project in it — the response then also carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution` (`{ Name, Path, SolutionFile }`) and `Status: Registered`. Pass `--skip-solution-registration` to opt out of both (Status `OptedOut`, bare single-nested layout). The success envelope always reports the outcome in `Data.SolutionRegistration`:
142	
143	```json
144	{
145	  "Result": "Success",
146	  "Code": "FlowInit",
147	  "Data": {
148	    "Status": "Created successfully",
149	    "Path": ".../<SolutionName>/<ProjectName>",
150	    "SolutionRegistration": {
151	      "Status": "Registered",                     // or "AlreadyRegistered"
152	      "Solution": ".../<SolutionName>.uipx",
153	      "Project": "<ProjectName>/project.uiproj",
154	      "ProjectId": "<uuid>"
155	    }
156	  }
157	}
158	```
159	
160	If `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` is `Registered` or `AlreadyRegistered`, **you are done** with this step — proceed to the layout check. If it is `OptedOut`, you passed `--skip-solution-registration` and the skip was intentional.
161	
162	**Fallback** — when `Status` is `Skipped` (ambiguous discovery — e.g. multiple `.uipx`), `Failed` (the `.uipx` write failed), or `NotInSolution` (rare — auto-scaffold did not run and no parent `.uipx` was found): wire the project manually.
163	
164	```bash
165	uip solution projects add \
166	  <directory>/<SolutionName>/<ProjectName> \
167	  <directory>/<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx
168	```

170	If you ended up with a bare single-nested layout (e.g. `--skip-solution-registration` was passed), **delete the partial scaffold and restart from Step 2a** — do not try to patch the layout by hand. See [diagnose/references/failure-modes.md — Single-nested layout](../../diagnose/references/failure-modes.md#single-nested-layout).

177	    ├── <SolutionName>.uipx
178	    └── <ProjectName>/                 ← from `uip maestro flow init` (run from inside <SolutionName>/)

261	
262	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-build-scaffold-assumptions:start-->
263	> **`flow init` scaffolds ONLY the manual trigger (`start` / `core.trigger.manual`) with zero edges.** Every other user-owned node — **including the End node** — is yours to add via `Edit` / `Write`. Any HTTP / connector / connector-trigger node you `node add`-ed in T1 is already in `nodes[]` and `definitions[]` but has empty `inputs.detail` (filled in T3) and is not wired yet.
264	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-build-scaffold-assumptions:end-->
265	
266	### T2 batch — issue these in ONE assistant message
267	
268	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:start-->
269	1. **One `Read`** of `<ProjectName>.flow` — required before any Edit/Write; T1's chained Bash mutated the file and Claude Code's file-state tracker does not auto-refresh on external mutations.
270	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:end-->
271	2. **A batch of parallel `Edit` calls** — one per top-level array you're modifying. Same-file Edits serialize in execution order, so each `old_string` must anchor to text NO OTHER parallel Edit modifies. Use the **per-array anchor pattern** below.
272	   - Edit `nodes[]` — add the End node (and any other user-owned nodes).
273	   - Edit `definitions[]` — paste the End definition verbatim from T1's `registry get core.control.end` output.
274	   - Edit `edges[]` — wire `trigger → <httpNode> → end`. End-node `outputs` mapping goes here too if you declared an `out` variable in `variables.globals`.
275	   - Edit `layout.nodes` — placeholder `{ position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, size: { width: 96, height: 96 }, collapsed: false }` per new node; `format` rewrites both position and size (by node shape) in T3.
276	
277	   `Write` of the whole file is allowed but token-costly on flows >~10 nodes — only fall back to `Write` when ≥70% of nodes change AND the file is small (see [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder)). **Never `Write` a flow that already has connector / connector-trigger / managed-HTTP nodes** — the rewrite clobbers their CLI-owned `bindings[]` / `inputs.detail` (invisible to `flow validate`); `Edit` in place, or re-run `node configure` as the last write. See [CAPABILITY.md — Node ownership](../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node).
278	
279	#### Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits — anchor on what you Read, not on key order
280	
281	> **Do not assume a top-level key order.** The CLI does not guarantee which keys are present or in what sequence — fixtures show `runtime` before `nodes` on one flow and absent on another, and `bindings` / `variables` / `solutionId` / `projectId` / `metadata` appear in varying positions. Any anchor of the form "closing `]` + the NEXT top-level key" is coupled to that ordering and will silently break across CLI versions or between flows. **Anchor on the target array's OWN key instead — you just `Read` the file at the top of T2, so anchor to text that read actually contains.**
282	
283	Anchor each Edit using its target array's own opening key, located in the text you just Read — not adjacency to a neighbor key. The catch: `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique in the file. They recur **inside inline `definitions[]`** (an HTTP v2 / agent / subprocess definition embeds its own nested `nodes`/`edges`) **and inside any `subflows.<id>` block** (each subflow holds its own `nodes`/`edges`) — so even a small flow can carry several copies. The reliable, version-independent discriminator is **indentation: the top-level array sits at 2-space indent; every nested one is deeper.** `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` appear once each, so they need no disambiguation.
284	
285	| Edit target | Anchor on (from the text you Read) | How to insert |
286	|---|---|---|
287	| Append to `nodes[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "nodes": [` (the top-level array — deeper-indented `"nodes": ["` inside definitions do not match the two-leading-space prefix) plus the `start` node's opening `{ "id": "start"`. | Insert the new node object as the first element, immediately after the `[`: `\n    { new node JSON },`. Head-insertion keeps `old_string` clear of the array's closing `]`. |
288	| Append to `edges[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "edges": [`. A newly generated scaffold commonly has `\n  "edges": []`; the 2-space prefix distinguishes it from nested `edges` arrays. | When empty, replace `\n  "edges": []` with `\n  "edges": [\n    { new edge JSON }\n  ]`. When non-empty, anchor through the first edge and insert the new edge as the first element. |
289	| Append to `definitions[]` | `"definitions": [` plus the first definition's opening bytes. Top-level `definitions[]` is the only one in the file, so this is reliably unique. | Insert the new definition right after the opening `[`, as the first element. Never anchor on whatever key follows `definitions` — that key varies (`runtime`, `bindings`, `variables`, `layout`, depending on CLI version and what the flow contains). |
290	| Add an entry to `layout.nodes` | `"layout": {\n    "nodes": {\n      "start":` — `start` is the always-present trigger and the first key under `layout.nodes` in newly generated flows. The top-level `"layout": {` is the only one. | `"layout":` + `"start":` jointly disambiguate. Insert `"<newId>": { ... },\n      ` before `"start":`. CLI-owned nodes added via `node add` already have a `layout.nodes` entry — only add entries for nodes you author by hand (e.g. End). |
291	
292	**Why head-insertion.** Inserting the new element right after the array's opening `[` means the `old_string` never includes the array's closing `]` — so it cannot collide with a closing `]` from a nested object (`form.sections[].fields[]`), and it never references a sibling top-level key whose position is not guaranteed. JSON array element order is not semantically significant for `nodes` / `edges` / `definitions`, so head vs. tail insertion is equivalent; `flow format` normalizes layout regardless.
293	
294	**Disjointness rule.** Two parallel Edits MUST anchor on DIFFERENT top-level arrays — nodes-Edit on the top-level `nodes[]`, edges-Edit on the top-level `edges[]`, definitions-Edit on `definitions[]`, layout-Edit on `layout.nodes`. Because each anchors on its own array (not a shared boundary), the parallel Edits never overlap — provided each anchor is unique first (see below).
295	
296	**Pre-flight uniqueness check.** Before submitting an Edit, confirm your `old_string` appears **exactly once** in the file you Read. `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` are reliably unique. `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT — they recur inside inline definitions and subflows, so anchor on the **2-space-indented** occurrence and extend through the first element's opening (e.g. `"id": "start"`) until the match count is one. Never anchor on a bare bracket shape, and never assume the first textual occurrence is the top-level one.
297	
298	**Safer fallback when in doubt:** serialize the Edits across two turns. One extra turn is cheaper than a failed-Edit recovery loop (which forces a re-Read, a re-derived anchor, and a re-submit).
299	
300	**Or skip the anchoring problem:** `scripts/flow_edit.py` and `scripts/flow_compose.py` parse the file and rewrite the arrays directly, so no `old_string` has to be unique. One call per node, edge, variable, or composite rewrite — see [editing-operations-json.md](editing-operations-json.md) for the per-operation flags. `Edit` remains the right tool for a small in-place value change you want to show as a diff.
301	
302	See [shared/file-format.md — Top-level structure](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure) for which top-level keys exist and the note that their order is not guaranteed.
303	
304	> **Intra-turn ordering.** If a parallel `Edit` fails with "file not read," split `Read` into its own turn (cost: +1 turn).
305	
306	### Node ownership recap
307	
308	> **Before each node, classify it as user-owned or CLI-owned (see [CAPABILITY.md — Node ownership](../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node)). Connector activities, connector triggers, and `core.action.http.v2` are CLI-only — use `uip maestro flow node add` + `uip maestro flow node configure`, never Edit. Hand-writing these will fail `flow validate`.**
309	
310	Edit `<ProjectName>.flow` directly in the project root. The `bindings_v2.json` file is also in the project root for resource bindings.
311	
312	> **Tool selection by ownership.** Use `Edit` for in-place changes to user-owned nodes; `Write` only when ≥70% of nodes change **and the flow has no CLI-owned nodes** (a full-file `Write` over connector / managed-HTTP nodes clobbers their `bindings[]` — see the Step 4 `Write` note above). For CLI-owned nodes (above), use `uip maestro flow node add` + `node configure` — see the relevant plugin's `impl.md` for the full configuration workflow. Inline-agent project scaffolding uses `uip agent init --inline-in-flow`, but inline-agent flow node/wiring edits are direct `.flow` JSON (the agent node itself is user-owned).
313	
314	Read [editing-operations.md](editing-operations.md) for strategy selection and per-operation recipes.
315	
316	> **Self-check before each mutation:** name the tool you're about to use. If the answer isn't `Edit`, `Write`, or `uip maestro flow ...` — STOP and ask the user (per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). `python`, `node`, `jq`, `sed`, `awk`, and shell heredocs are a last resort and require explicit user approval after you've surfaced the trade-offs. See [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder).
317	
318	For each node type, follow the relevant plugin's `impl.md` for node-specific inputs, JSON structure, and configuration. The operations guides cover the mechanics (how to add/remove/wire); the plugins cover the semantics (what inputs and model fields each node type needs).
319	
320	## Step 5 — Validate **[T3 — chain with Step 6, plus any T1 `node configure`]**
321	
322	### Canonical T3 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
323	
324	```bash
325	uip maestro flow node configure "<ProjectName>.flow" "<httpNodeId>" --detail '<DETAIL_JSON>' --output json \
326	  && uip maestro flow validate "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json \
327	  && uip maestro flow format "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json
328	```
329	
330	`<DETAIL_JSON>` is node-type-specific — the schema is owned by each CLI-owned node's plugin, not duplicated here: HTTP → [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md#critical-use-node-configure), connectors → [connector/impl.md](plugins/connector/impl.md), connector triggers → [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md). Tail-append one `node configure` per CLI-owned node added in T1, using the node IDs captured from T1's chained output. Drop the entire `node configure` segment if no CLI-owned nodes exist.
331	
332	> **The plugin `impl.md` is authoritative — follow its full procedure, not just its `--detail` schema, and let it override this turn map.** A plugin may prescribe steps the three-turn collapse does not show — most importantly a **pre-`configure` live fetch** whose output you must read before you can author `--detail` (the value depends on the live response, so it cannot be guessed or copied from a doc example). When `impl.md` defines such a step, run it in its **own turn before T3** and build `--detail` from its result; do not batch it into the chain, skip it, or hand-author the payload. An empty or static base response is expected for these steps and is not a signal the step is unavailable. This is general to every CLI-owned node type — defer to the owning `impl.md` rather than assuming static config.
333	
334	Chain `python3 scripts/audit_flow.py "<ProjectName>.flow"` into the same call, before `validate` — it reports the defects `validate` does not catch (wiring, `=js:` fields, Jint constructs, resource bindings, runtime gaps) while you are still in T3.
335	
336	**On validate failure:** one `Edit` turn to fix, then re-chain `validate && format` in one Bash. Do not validate after every individual Edit during T2 — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
337	
338	> **A passing exit code with warnings is NOT done.** `flow validate` returns 0 even when `Data.Warnings` is non-empty — read the warnings, don't just check the exit code. The connector-keyword warning (`node "…" mentions the "<connector>" connector keyword but uses the generic Managed HTTP type core.action.http.v2 with no connection binding`) means the flow took the brand-name shortcut and will run against an undefined endpoint at debug time — resolve it by switching to the connector before reporting the flow complete (see [SKILL.md rule #3](../../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) and the anti-pattern list). Treat this class of warning as a build failure for your own definition of "done."
339	
340	### Common error categories
341	
342	- **Missing targetPort** — every edge needs a `targetPort` string
343	- **Missing definition** — every `type:typeVersion` in nodes needs a matching `definitions` entry
344	- **Invalid node/edge references** — `sourceNodeId`/`targetNodeId` must reference existing node `id`s
345	- **Duplicate IDs** — node and edge `id`s must be unique
346	
347	## Step 6 — Format node layout **[T3 — chained tail of Step 5]**
348	
349	This is the last segment of the [canonical T3 chain](#canonical-t3-chain--issue-this-as-one-bash-call) above. After validation passes, format must run before publishing or debugging (see "Always run `flow format` after edits" in [the Author capability index](../CAPABILITY.md)). Format:
350	
351	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) using ELK with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
352	- Sets each non-stickyNote node's `size` by its canvas shape so Studio Web renders it correctly: inline agents (`shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`, containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`, everything else (incl. referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>`) → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }` (skipping this leaves stale dimensions intact and produces misshapen nodes — the MST-9061 failure mode)
353	- Recurses into subflows and rewrites `subflows[<id>].layout`
354	- Backfills missing `position`/`size` entries
355	
356	Standalone (only if not chained from Step 5):
357	
358	```bash
359	uip maestro flow format <ProjectName>.flow --output json
360	```
361	
362	## Completion Output
363	
364	When you finish building the flow, report to the user:
365	
366	1. **File path** of the `.flow` file created
367	2. **What was built** — summary of nodes added, edges wired, and logic implemented
368	3. **Validation status** — whether `flow validate` passes (or remaining errors if unresolvable)
369	4. **Format status** — confirm `flow format` was run
370	5. **Mock placeholders** — list any `core.logic.mock` nodes that need to be replaced, and which skill to use
371	6. **Missing connections** — any connector nodes that need connections the user must create
372	7. **What's next** — ask the user, presenting the dropdown below (see the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md))
373	
374	### What's next dropdown
375	
376	Authoring terminates here. Each option below hands off to Operate — read [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../../operate/CAPABILITY.md) for the command sequence.
377	
378	| Option | What it does |
379	| --- | --- |
380	| **Publish to Studio Web** (default) | Push the solution to Studio Web so the user can visualize, edit, and publish from the browser. |
381	| **Debug the solution** | Execute the flow end-to-end against real systems. Confirm consent first — debug has real side effects (see the consent-before-debug rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). |
382	| **Deploy to Orchestrator** | Pack and publish directly to Orchestrator (bypasses Studio Web). Only when explicitly chosen — see [/uipath:uipath-platform](/uipath:uipath-platform). |
383	| **Something else** | Last option. Accept free-form string input and act on it (e.g., "just leave it", "pack but don't publish", "upload to a different tenant"). |
384	
385	Do not run any of these actions without explicit user selection. Once the user picks an option, read [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../../operate/CAPABILITY.md) and follow that capability's flow — do not run operate commands from inside this doc.

1 # Variables and Expressions 2 3 Complete reference for declaring variables, writing expressions, and managing data flow in `.flow` files. 4 5 > **Read this before** adding variables or writing expressions in any flow. 6 > 7 > `flow validate` catches the structural expression-reference errors: 8 > 9 > - Missing `=js:` prefix on `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` (MST-9107) 10 > - Invented `nodes..output` syntax 11 > - References to unknown variables or node IDs 12 > - Output-path walks that descend into declared primitives or schemas closed with `additionalProperties: false` 13 > 14 > Errors against **open output schemas** (HTTP response bodies, script returns, free-text agent output) and **wrong-direction reads** (e.g. reading an `out`-only variable) still slip past validate and surface only at `flow debug` or in production. 15 16 --- 17 18 ## Table of contents 19 20 - [Variables Overview](#variables-overview) 21 - [Workflow Variables (`globals`)](#workflow-variables-globals) 22 - [Node Variables (`nodes`)](#node-variables-nodes) 23 - [Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`)](#variable-updates-variableupdates) 24 - [Output Mapping on End Nodes](#output-mapping-on-end-nodes) 25 - [Expression System](#expression-system) 26 - [Available Globals](#available-globals) 27 - [Expression Contexts](#expression-contexts) 28 - [Jint Engine Constraints](#jint-engine-constraints) 29 - [Scoping Rules](#scoping-rules) 30 - [Variable Management via CLI](#variable-management-via-cli) 31 - [Complete Example](#complete-example) 32 33 --- 34 35 ## Variables Overview 36 37 Every flow has a `variables` object at the top level of the `.flow` file. It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. 1	# Wiring Node Outputs to Downstream Inputs
2	
3	How to reference one node's output (or any `$vars.*` value) from another node's input fields. This is the **single source of truth** for `=js:` expression rules in `.flow` JSON. All node-type plugins (connector, http, script, decision, end, etc.) defer to this file.
4	
5	> **Read this before** writing any field that needs to reference a previous node's output, a workflow variable, or any other `$vars.*` / `$metadata.*` value. Skipping `=js:` is the #1 cause of "the value at runtime was the literal string `vars.X.output.Id`" failures (MST-9107).
6	
7	---
8	
9	## The Rule (one sentence)
10	
11	**Any string that references `$vars.*`, `$metadata.*`, or `$self.*` MUST start with `=js:`. Otherwise it is a literal string at runtime.**
12	
13	---
14	
15	## What Goes Wrong Without `=js:`
16	
17	The Flow runtime serializes string fields into BPMN. The serializer rewrites the canvas-form tokens (`$vars` → `vars`) **whether or not the `=js:` prefix is present**. This means a missing prefix is silent — `flow validate` passes, the file looks plausible, but at runtime the BPMN engine sees a plain string and never evaluates it.
18	
19	Three failure modes observed in agent-generated `.flow` files:
20	
21	| What the agent wrote | What ships to runtime | Result |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `"nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | Literal string — invented `nodes.` prefix has no meaning. |
24	| `"$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | Literal string — `$vars` rewritten to `vars` but no `=js:` so never evaluated. |
25	| `"=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"=js:vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | Evaluates correctly. |
26	
27	**There is no "nodes.X.output.Y" syntax.** Variable references always use `$vars.*`.
28	
29	---
30	
31	## The Canonical Pattern
32	
33	```
34	"=js:$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output.<field>"
35	```
36	
37	- `<sourceNodeId>` — the `id` value of the node that produces the output
38	- `output` — the literal string `output` (the standard output port; use `error` for errors)
39	- `<field>` — the field path within the output object
40	
41	### Examples
42	
43	| What you want | Expression |
44	|---|---|
45	| The whole output object | `=js:$vars.fetchUser1.output` |
46	| One field from a single-record output | `=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id` |
47	| A field from the first record of a query result (array) | `=js:$vars.queryEntityRecords1.output[0].Id` |
48	| Filter on a value from a previous node | `=js:$vars.fetchUser1.output.id === $vars.input.userId` |
49	| A static value (no variables) | `"HDFC Bank"` (no prefix needed) |
50	| A built-in metadata value | `=js:$metadata.instanceId` |
51	| A literal that contains a variable | `` =js:`Hello ${$vars.userName}` `` |
52	
53	---
54	
55	## Where the Rule Applies
56	
57	`=js:` is **required** in every field below when the value references `$vars`, `$metadata`, or `$self`:
58	
59	| Node / context | Field | Required `=js:`? |
60	|---|---|---|
61	| **Connector activity nodes** (`uipath.connector.<connector-key>.<activity>`) | `inputs.detail.bodyParameters.*` (all values) | **YES** |
62	| | `inputs.detail.queryParameters.*` (all values) | **YES** |
63	| | `inputs.detail.pathParameters.*` (all values) | **YES** |
64	| **Managed HTTP** (`core.action.http.v2`) | `inputs.detail.bodyParameters.url` / `headers` / `query` / `body` — both manual and connector mode store dynamic fields here in the `.flow` JSON, regardless of how the CLI's `--detail` flag accepts them at the top level | **YES** |
65	| **Custom HTTP** (`core.action.http`) | `inputs.url` / `headers` / `body` / `queryParams` (deprecated; prefer `core.action.http.v2`) | **YES** |
66	| **HTTP branches** | `inputs.branches[].conditionExpression` | **NO** — already JS, do not prefix |
67	| **Decision** (`core.logic.decision`) | `inputs.expression` | **NO** — already JS, do not prefix |
68	| **Switch** (`core.logic.switch`) | `inputs.cases[].expression` | **NO** — already JS, do not prefix |
69	| **End nodes** (`core.control.end`) | `outputs.<varId>.source` | **YES** |
70	| **Variable updates** | `variables.variableUpdates.<nodeId>[].expression` | **YES** (the CLI auto-prefixes if missing, but write it explicitly) |
71	| **Loop nodes** (`core.logic.loop`) | `inputs.collection` | **YES** |
72	| **Subflow nodes** (`core.subflow`) | `inputs.<inputId>.source` | **YES** |
73	| **Script nodes** (`core.action.script`) | `inputs.script` body — `$vars.*` is read inside JS, no `=js:` wrapping | **NO** — the body is already JS |
74	| **Inline-agent prompt** (`uipath.agent.autonomous` `agent.json` `messages[].content`) | Tokens reference upstream flow nodes directly: `{{ $vars.<flowNodeId>.output[.<field>] }}` (spaced braces). Mirror in `contentTokens[]` as `{ "type": "variable", "rawString": " $vars.<flowNodeId>.output[.<field>] " }` — `rawString` must include leading and trailing space. Never `{{input.<id>}}` and never bare `{{name}}`. | **NO** — `{{ ... }}` tokens, not `=js:`. See [author/references/plugins/inline-agent/impl.md § Wiring Flow Variables into Agent Prompts](../author/references/plugins/inline-agent/impl.md#wiring-flow-variables-into-agent-prompts). |
75	
76	**Rule of thumb:** If the field is *value-typed* (anything other than a hardcoded condition), `=js:` is required for `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` references. The two condition fields (Decision, Switch) and the script body are the only exceptions — they are always parsed as JS regardless.
77	
78	---
79	
80	## Connector Node Wiring — Quick Reference
81	
82	For connector nodes (`uipath.connector.*`), the most common wiring patterns:
83	
84	```jsonc
85	"inputs": {
86	  "detail": {
87	    "method": "POST",
88	    "endpoint": "/v2/{entityName}/UpdateEntityRecord",
89	    "pathParameters": {
90	      "entityName": "BankDetails"
91	    },
92	    "queryParameters": {
93	      "recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id",
94	      "expansionLevel": "3"
95	    },
96	    "bodyParameters": {
97	      "BankName": "HDFC Bank",
98	      "AccountId": "=js:$vars.queryAccounts1.output[0].Id",
99	      "Notes": "=js:`Created from flow run ${$metadata.instanceId}`"
100	    }
101	  }
102	}
103	```
104	
105	- **Static values** (`"HDFC Bank"`, `"3"`) — no prefix, written as plain JSON values.
106	- **Variable references** (`$vars.X.output.Y`) — **always** wrap with `=js:`.
107	- **Mixed strings** (template literals) — wrap the whole expression in `=js:` and use JS template literal syntax with `${ }`.
108	
109	Plugin-specific path fields are not value fields. **Always** follow the plugin reference when it says a field stores a path string. Notable exception: Transform `inputs.collection` must be a path such as `"$vars.orders.output.items"`, without `=js:`.
110	
111	---
112	
113	## Anti-Patterns (Never Write These)
114	
115	1. **Never invent a `nodes.X.output.Y` syntax.** It does not exist. All variable references use `$vars`.
116	2. **Never write `$vars.X.output.Y` without `=js:`** in an expression value field. The `$vars→vars` rewrite happens regardless of prefix, leaving you with a literal string `"vars.X.output.Y"` at runtime — looks like an expression, isn't one. For plugin path fields such as Transform `inputs.collection`, use the plugin-specific path format instead.
117	3. **Never wrap conditions** (Decision, Switch, HTTP branch) in `=js:`. Those are parsed as JS automatically.
118	4. **Never use `{ }` template interpolation in connector or HTTP activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner skips these fields. The `$` is stripped and `{vars.X}` ships literally to the IS runtime. Use `=js:` and JS template literals (`` `…${$vars.X}…` ``) instead.
119	5. **Never quote `=js:` itself in an expression.** `"=js:$vars.X"` is correct. `"\"=js:$vars.X\""` is a string containing the prefix.
120	
121	---
122	
123	## Why The Engine Works This Way
124	
125	The flow-workbench serializer (`expression-transform.ts`) walks every string in node data and rewrites `$vars` → `vars` so the BPMN runtime sees engine-form tokens. It does **not** check for the `=js:` prefix when doing this rewrite — the prefix is what tells the BPMN engine to actually evaluate the result as JavaScript. Without it, the BPMN engine treats the string as a literal value and binds it to the activity input as-is.
126	
127	For variable updates only, `bpmn-moddle.ts` has a fallback (`ensureJsPrefix`) that warns and auto-prefixes. There is **no equivalent fallback for connector/HTTP activity inputs** — values pass through verbatim. Always include `=js:` explicitly.
128	
129	---
130	
131	## Validation Tip
132	
133	When debugging a flow whose output is the literal string `vars.X.output.Y` (or `nodes.X.output.Y`, or any other unevaluated expression) instead of the expected value:
134	
135	1. Run `python3 scripts/audit_expressions.py <project>.flow`. It walks every string in `nodes[].inputs` / `nodes[].outputs` and `variables.variableUpdates` and applies the table above per node type and field path, reporting `MISSING_JS_PREFIX`, `JS_ON_CONDITION`, `INVENTED_NODES_SYNTAX`, `BRACE_INTERPOLATION` and `QUOTED_JS_PREFIX` with the exact JSON path. `--format json` for machine-readable findings; exit 1 when anything is wrong. A `$vars` reference in a field this table does not cover is reported as a warning, because a plugin may document that field as a path (see the Transform `inputs.collection` note above) — decide per plugin.
136	2. Fix each reported path: prepend `=js:` in value fields, drop it from condition fields.
137	3. Re-run the audit, then `uip maestro flow validate`, then re-debug.

3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.logic.loop`
6	
7	## Registry Validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.loop --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input ports `input` and `loopBack`, output ports `success` and `output`, required input `collection`. Set the node instance `typeVersion` to the `version` field from this response — do not hardcode it.
14	
15	## JSON Structure
16	
17	### Loop node
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "id": "loop1",
22	  "type": "core.logic.loop",
23	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
24	  "display": { "label": "Loop over items" },
25	  "inputs": {
26	    "collection": "=js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items",
27	    "parallel": false
28	  }
29	}
30	```
31	
32	> **Collection source shape depends on the node type.** Connector `list` activities return the bare array — `"collection": "=js:$vars.searchIssuesByJql1.output"`, NOT `.output.issues` / `.output.items`. HTTP nodes differ — envelope preserved: `.output.body.<key>` as above. See [connector/impl.md — Connector output shape](../connector/impl.md).
33	
34	Set `"parallel": true` to execute all iterations concurrently.
35	
36	### Loop body nodes — `parentId` required
37	
38	Every node inside the loop body **must** have `"parentId"` set to the loop node's ID. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is part of the loop and variableUpdates will not fire per-iteration.
39	
40	```json
41	{
42	  "id": "processItem",
43	  "type": "core.action.script",
44	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
45	  "display": { "label": "Process item" },
46	  "inputs": {
47	    "script": "return $vars.product * $vars.loop1.currentItem"
48	  },
49	  "parentId": "loop1"
50	}
51	```
52	
53	> **Critical:** If you omit `parentId`, the node executes outside the loop context. State variables will not update across iterations and loop outputs like `currentItem` will be inaccessible.
54	
55	## Adding / Editing
56	
57	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Use the JSON structure above for the node-specific `inputs` and `parentId`.

61	When adding a CLI carve-out node (connector, connector trigger, or managed HTTP) inside a loop, pass `--parent` to set `parentId` automatically:

71	
72	Loop nodes have a specific wiring pattern:

75	- `output` — into the loop body (first body node)
76	- `loopBack` — return from last body node back to loop
77	- `success` — exit after loop completes (to next downstream node)
78	
79	See [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md) for edge add procedures.
80	
81	## Accessing Loop Variables Inside Body
82	
83	Inside the loop body, access the current item via `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem`:
84	
85	```javascript
86	// In a Script node inside the loop body (parentId must be set to the loop node)
87	const item = $vars.loop1.currentItem;
88	const index = $vars.loop1.currentIndex;
89	return { processed: item.name.toUpperCase(), position: index };
90	```
91	
92	| Variable | Description |
93	| --- | --- |
94	| `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` | The item being processed in this iteration |
95	| `$vars.<loopId>.currentIndex` | 0-based iteration index |
96	| `$vars.<loopId>.collection` | The full collection being iterated |
97	
98	> **Do not use `iterator.currentItem`.** The correct access pattern is `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` where `<loopId>` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`).
99	
100	### Required node variables for loop outputs
101	
102	For `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` etc. to resolve, you must add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`:
103	
104	```json
105	{
106	  "variables": {
107	    "nodes": [
108	      {
109	        "id": "loop1.currentItem",
110	        "type": "any",
111	        "description": "The current item being iterated in the loop",
112	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentItem" }
113	      },
114	      {
115	        "id": "loop1.currentIndex",
116	        "type": "number",
117	        "description": "The current iteration index (0-based)",
118	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentIndex" }
119	      },
120	      {
121	        "id": "loop1.collection",
122	        "type": "array",
123	        "description": "The collection being iterated over",
124	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "collection" }
125	      },
126	      {
127	        "id": "loop1.output",
128	        "type": "array",
129	        "description": "Aggregated results from all loop iterations",
130	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "output" }
131	      }
132	    ]
133	  }
134	}
135	```
136	
137	## State Accumulation with variableUpdates
138	
139	To accumulate state across loop iterations (counters, running totals), use an `inout` variable with a `variableUpdate` on the body node:
140	
141	```json
142	{
143	  "variables": {
144	    "globals": [
145	      {
146	        "id": "runningTotal",
147	        "direction": "inout",
148	        "type": "number",
149	        "defaultValue": 0
150	      }
151	    ],
152	    "variableUpdates": {
153	      "bodyNode": [
154	        {
155	          "variableId": "runningTotal",
156	          "expression": "=js:$vars.bodyNode.output"
157	        }
158	      ]
159	    }
160	  }
161	}
162	```
163	
164	The variableUpdate fires after each iteration, so the `inout` variable carries the accumulated value into the next iteration.
165	
166	> **Critical:** The variableUpdate expression **cannot** access loop iteration variables like `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem`. These are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). If you need to compute using `currentItem`, do the computation in the script and reference the script's output in the variableUpdate.
167	
168	## Complete Example — Loop with State Accumulation
169	
170	A flow that iterates over a collection, accumulates a result in an `inout` variable via a Script body node, and outputs the final value.
171	
172	```json
173	{
174	  "nodes": [
175	    {
176	      "id": "start",
177	      "type": "core.trigger.manual",
178	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
179	      "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
180	      "inputs": { "entryPointId": "..." }
181	    },
182	    {
183	      "id": "loop1",
184	      "type": "core.logic.loop",
185	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
186	      "display": { "label": "Loop" },
187	      "inputs": { "collection": "=js:$vars.inputItems", "parallel": false }
188	    },
189	    {
190	      "id": "bodyScript",
191	      "type": "core.action.script",
192	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
193	      "display": { "label": "Process item" },
194	      "inputs": {
195	        "script": "return $vars.accumulator + $vars.loop1.currentItem;"
196	      },
197	      "parentId": "loop1"
198	    },
199	    {
200	      "id": "end1",
201	      "type": "core.control.end",
202	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
203	      "display": { "label": "End" },
204	      "inputs": {},
205	      "outputs": {
206	        "result": { "source": "=js:$vars.accumulator" }
207	      }
208	    }
209	  ],
210	  "edges": [
211	    { "id": "e1", "sourceNodeId": "start", "sourcePort": "output", "targetNodeId": "loop1", "targetPort": "input" },
212	    { "id": "e2", "sourceNodeId": "loop1", "sourcePort": "output", "targetNodeId": "bodyScript", "targetPort": "input" },
213	    { "id": "e3", "sourceNodeId": "bodyScript", "sourcePort": "success", "targetNodeId": "loop1", "targetPort": "loopBack" },
214	    { "id": "e4", "sourceNodeId": "loop1", "sourcePort": "success", "targetNodeId": "end1", "targetPort": "input" }
215	  ],
216	  "variables": {
217	    "globals": [
218	      { "id": "inputItems", "direction": "in", "type": "array", "defaultValue": [] },
219	      { "id": "accumulator", "direction": "inout", "type": "number", "defaultValue": 0 },
220	      { "id": "result", "direction": "out", "type": "number" }
221	    ],
222	    "nodes": [
223	      { "id": "loop1.currentItem", "type": "any", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentItem" } },
224	      { "id": "loop1.currentIndex", "type": "number", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentIndex" } },
225	      { "id": "loop1.collection", "type": "array", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "collection" } },
226	      { "id": "loop1.output", "type": "array", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "output" } },
227	      { "id": "bodyScript.output", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "bodyScript", "outputId": "output" } },
228	      { "id": "bodyScript.error", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "bodyScript", "outputId": "error" } }
229	    ],
230	    "variableUpdates": {
231	      "bodyScript": [
232	        { "variableId": "accumulator", "expression": "=js:$vars.bodyScript.output" }
233	      ]
234	    }
235	  }
236	}
237	```
238	
239	Key points in this pattern:
240	- `bodyScript` has `"parentId": "loop1"` — places it inside the loop
241	- Script accesses `$vars.loop1.currentItem` for the current iteration value
242	- `variableUpdate` on `bodyScript` writes the script's return value back to `accumulator`
243	- `accumulator` is `inout` so it persists across iterations
244	- End node maps the final accumulated value to the `out` variable
245	
246	## Complete Example — Multi-Node Loop Body (HTTP + Script)
247	
248	Loop over items, fetch data per-iteration via HTTP, process with a script. Both body nodes have `parentId`.

274	      "display": { "label": "Fetch data" },
275	      "inputs": { "branches": [], "timeout": "PT15M", "retryCount": 0, "detail": {} },
276	      "parentId": "loop1"
277	    },

281	      "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
282	      "display": { "label": "Process item" },

284	        "script": "return { name: $vars.loop1.currentItem.name, value: $vars.fetchData1.output.body.result };"
285	      },

296	  ],

299	    { "id": "e2", "sourceNodeId": "loop1", "sourcePort": "start", "targetNodeId": "fetchData1", "targetPort": "input" },

303	  ],
304	  "variables": {
305	    "globals": [
306	      { "id": "results", "direction": "out", "type": "array" }
307	    ],
308	    "nodes": [
309	      { "id": "loop1.currentItem", "type": "any", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentItem" } },
310	      { "id": "loop1.currentIteration", "type": "number", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentIteration" } },
311	      { "id": "loop1.collection", "type": "array", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "collection" } },
312	      { "id": "loop1.output", "type": "array", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "output" } },
313	      { "id": "fetchData1.output", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "fetchData1", "outputId": "output" } },
314	      { "id": "fetchData1.error", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "fetchData1", "outputId": "error" } },

322	- Both `fetchData1` and `processItem1` have `"parentId": "loop1"` — omitting it on either causes null outputs at runtime while validation passes
323	- HTTP body uses `start`/`default` ports; script returns via `success`/`continue`
324	- `detail` on HTTP node is abbreviated — populate via `uip maestro flow node configure`
325	
326	## Debug
327	
328	| Error | Cause | Fix |
329	| --- | --- | --- |
330	| Collection is empty or null | Expression evaluates to null/undefined | Check `collection` expression and upstream output |
331	| `$vars.loop1.currentItem` is undefined | Missing node variable binding or missing `parentId` | Add `loop1.currentItem` to `variables.nodes` and set `parentId` on body nodes |
332	| State variable not updating across iterations | Body node missing `parentId` | Add `"parentId": "<loopId>"` to every node inside the loop body |
333	| State variable becomes `NaN` | variableUpdate expression uses `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` | Loop variables are not available in variableUpdate expressions. Do the computation in the script and reference `$vars.<bodyNodeId>.output` in the variableUpdate |
334	| Infinite loop | Edges wired incorrectly | Ensure only `loopBack` creates the cycle, not arbitrary edges |
335	| No output after loop | Missing `success` edge | Wire the `success` port to the next downstream node |

1	# Loop Node — Planning
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.logic.loop`
6	
7	## When to Use
8	
9	Use a Loop node to iterate over a collection of items. Supports sequential and parallel execution.
10	
11	### Selection Heuristics
12	
13	| Situation | Use Loop? |
14	| --- | --- |
15	| Process each item in an array | Yes |
16	| Run the same operation on multiple inputs concurrently | Yes (with `parallel: true`) |
17	| Simple data transformation on a collection | No — use [Transform](../transform/planning.md) |
18	| Distribute work items to robots | No — use [Queue](../queue/planning.md) |
19	
20	## Ports
21	
22	| Input Port(s) | Output Port(s) |
23	| --- | --- |
24	| `input`, `loopBack` | `success`, `output`, `error` |
25	
26	- `loopBack` — receives the edge returning from the last node inside the loop body
27	- `success` — fires after all iterations complete
28	- `output` — carries aggregated results from all iterations
29	- `error` — implicit error port shared with all action nodes; fires when the loop or an iteration throws. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
30	
31	## Key Inputs
32	
33	| Input | Required | Description |
34	| --- | --- | --- |
35	| `collection` | Yes | Expression pointing to an array (e.g., `$vars.fetchData.output.body.items`) |
36	| `parallel` | No | `true` to execute all iterations concurrently (default: sequential) |
37	
38	## Loop Variables (available inside loop body only)
39	
40	- `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` — the item being processed in this iteration
41	- `$vars.<loopId>.currentIndex` — 0-based iteration index
42	- `$vars.<loopId>.collection` — the full collection
43	
44	Where `<loopId>` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`).
45	
46	## Wiring Rules
47	
48	- The loop body starts from the `output` port of the loop node
49	- The last node in the loop body connects back to the loop's `loopBack` port
50	- After all iterations, execution continues from the `success` port
51	- Do not create cycles except through the `loopBack` mechanism
52	- **Every node inside the loop body must have `"parentId": "<loopId>"`** — without this, variableUpdates will not fire per-iteration and loop variables will be inaccessible
53

1	# Script Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.action.script`
6	
7	## Registry validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input port `input`, output port `success`, required input `script` (string, non-empty). See [Action Node Structure — Registry validation](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#registry-validation) for the shared pattern.
14	
15	## JSON structure
16	
17	Follow the [Action Node Structure — Standard JSON skeleton](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#standard-json-skeleton). The script-specific input is a single `script` string:
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "inputs": {
22	    "script": "const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;\nconst total = items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.amount, 0);\nreturn { total, count: items.length };"
23	  }
24	}
25	```
26	
27	## Adding and editing
28	
29	See [Action Node Structure — Adding and editing procedures](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#adding-and-editing-procedures). The script node uses the standard input port `input` and output port `success`; no plugin-specific wiring.
30	
31	## Script rules
32	
33	1. **Top-level body — no `function main()` wrapper.** Node runs the `script` text directly (as a function body); a wrapper is never called → `output` null. Read workflow variables via `$vars.<variableId>` and upstream node outputs via `$vars.<nodeId>.output`; end with top-level `return {…}`. Not a coded Function: no `main`, no injected args.
34	   - Correct: `const n = $vars.ixp1.output.field; return { n };`
35	   - Wrong: `function main({ ixp1 }) { … }`
36	2. **Must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar. The return value becomes `$vars.<nodeId>.output`.
37	3. **`$vars` is a global** — use it directly: `return { upper: $vars.customerName.toUpperCase() }`
38	4. **JavaScript ES2020 (Jint engine)** — see [variables-and-expressions.md](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for supported features and Jint constraints.
39	5. **No `console.log`** — `console` is not available. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
40	6. **No external calls** — use the HTTP node or a connector node for API calls.
41	7. **30-second timeout** — long-running computations will be killed.
42	8. **Never name a variable `aggregate`** — reserved host global. On any `Identifier 'X' has already been declared`, rename `X`.
43	
44	**Script:** `python3 scripts/lint_jint.py <ProjectName>.flow` checks rules 1, 2, 5, 6 and 8 above (plus the wider unsupported-construct list) across every script node and `=js:` expression in the file. The 30-second timeout is a runtime property and is not statically checkable.
45	
46	## Common patterns
47	
48	### Transform and return
49	
50	```javascript
51	const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;
52	const filtered = items.filter(i => i.status === "active");
53	return { items: filtered, count: filtered.length };
54	```
55	
56	### Build a payload for a downstream node
57	
58	```javascript
59	return {
60	  subject: `Order ${$vars.orderId} - Confirmation`,
61	  body: `Your order of ${$vars.orderTotal} has been processed.`,
62	  recipient: $vars.customerEmail
63	};
64	```
65	
66	### Error check from upstream
67	
68	```javascript
69	const error = $vars.httpCall.error;
70	if (error) {
71	  return { hasError: true, message: error.message };
72	}
73	return { hasError: false, data: $vars.httpCall.output.body };
74	```
75	
76	### Reading a file-typed variable
77	
78	A `file` variable (bound via `uip maestro flow debug --attachment <id>=<path>`) hydrates as an **object**, not a string. Read the uploaded file's name from `.FullName`:
79	
80	```javascript
81	const doc = $vars.start.output.inputDoc; // file variable → object
82	return { fileName: doc.FullName };        // .FullName, not .name/.fileName
83	```
84	
85	Property access is **case-sensitive** — these casings resolve: `.FullName`, `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.MimeType`, `.Metadata.size` (nested, lowercase `size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do not exist. See [variables-and-expressions.md — Runtime shape of a `file` variable](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md#file-input).
86	
87	## Debug
88	
89	| Error | Cause | Fix |
90	| --- | --- | --- |
91	| Script did not return a value | Missing `return` statement | Add `return { ... }` |
92	| `output` is `null` but script has a `return` | `return` is inside an uncalled `function main(){}` wrapper | Remove wrapper; code + `return` at top level (rule 1) |
93	| Return value is not an object | Returned a scalar (`return 42`) | Wrap in object: `return { value: 42 }` |
94	| `$vars.nodeId` is undefined | Upstream node not connected or wrong ID | Check edges and node IDs |
95	| Timeout after 30s | Script too expensive | Simplify logic or split into multiple scripts |
96	| `console is not defined` | Used `console.log()` | Remove — use `return { debug: val }` instead |
97	| `fetch is not defined` | Tried to make HTTP call | Use an HTTP node or connector node instead |
98	| `[300501] Error invoking script task` with `Unexpected token` | Malformed JavaScript — `flow validate` does not parse script bodies, so syntax errors surface only at runtime. Common slip: one missing `)` in chained `(((a \|\| {}).b \|\| {}).c \|\| [])` guards | Balance parentheses; check with `node -e "new Function(<script>)"` before validate |
99	| `Identifier 'X' has already been declared` | `X` collides with a runtime-injected global (known: `aggregate`) | Rename `X` (e.g. `agg`) |
100

1	# End Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.control.end`
6	
7	## Registry Validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.control.end --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input port `input`, no output ports. Set the node instance `typeVersion` to the `version` field from this response — do not hardcode it.
14	
15	## JSON Structure
16	
17	### Without Output Mapping
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "id": "doneSuccess",
22	  "type": "core.control.end",
23	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
24	  "display": { "label": "Done" },
25	  "inputs": {}
26	}
27	```
28	
29	### With Output Mapping
30	
31	When the workflow declares `out` variables, every End node must map all of them:
32	
33	```json
34	{
35	  "id": "doneSuccess",
36	  "type": "core.control.end",
37	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
38	  "display": { "label": "Done" },
39	  "inputs": {},
40	  "outputs": {
41	    "processedCount": {
42	      "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output.count"
43	    },
44	    "resultSummary": {
45	      "source": "=js:$vars.formatOutput.output.summary"
46	    }
47	  }
48	}
49	```
50	
51	Each key in `outputs` must match a variable `id` from `variables.globals` where `direction: "out"`.
52	
53	## Adding / Editing
54	
55	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Use the JSON structure above for the node-specific `inputs` and `outputs`.
56	
57	Output mapping must be added with `Edit` against the `.flow` file — see [Edit/Write: Add output mapping](../../editing-operations-json.md#add-output-mapping-on-an-end-node).
58	
59	## Debug
60	
61	| Error | Cause | Fix |
62	| --- | --- | --- |
63	| Missing output mapping | `out` variable not mapped on this End node | Add `outputs.{varId}.source` expression for every `out` variable |
64	| Output expression unresolvable | `$vars` reference points to unreachable node | Ensure the node is upstream and connected via edges |
65	| Runtime silent failure | Output mapping missing on one reachable End node | Check **all** End nodes, not just the primary path |
